lessons.title: 要不是 (yàobúshì) — if it were not for

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for the whole chain of causes, then the Mandarin for what is going on here.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: 要不是

segments.text: 要不是 — yàobúshì — "if it were not for".
要不是你我们就找不到这儿了 yàobúshì nǐ wǒmen jiù zhǎo bu dào zhèr le — If it weren't for you, we'd never have found this place.
Tone: 不 is said bú before the falling tone of shì, and the spelling shows it.

要不是 (yàobúshì) is built from 要 'if', 不 'not' and 是 'to be', all inherited from Middle Chinese, 'jiewH, pjut and dzyeX (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription); the dictionary glosses the first 'to bind by agreement', and its use for 'if' is not given there.
One more word for saying what would happen.

lessons.title: duōkuī — it is thanks to; luckily for
lessons.gloss: it is thanks to; luckily for

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for what is going on here, then the Mandarin for if it were not for.
duōkuī — "it is thanks to; luckily for".
duōkuī nǐ bāng wǒ bùrán wǒ jiù zuò bu wán — Thanks to your help I finished; otherwise I'd never have managed.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

duōkuī is built from 多 'much' and kuī, both inherited from Middle Chinese, ta and khjwe (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'many' and the second 'to be lacking'. How the pair came to mean 'thanks to' is not settled.
One more word for saying what would happen.

gǎishàn — "to make conditions better".
zhǐyào dàjiā yìqǐ nǔlì huánjìng jiù huì gǎishàn — As long as we all work together, the environment will get better.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

gǎishàn is built from 改 'to change' and shàn 'good', both inherited from Middle Chinese, kojX and dzyenX (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to alter' and the second 'good'.
One more word for saying what would happen.

zhǔyào — "main; chief".
wǒ bú qù de zhǔyào yuányīn shì tiānqì bù hǎo — The main reason I'm not going is the bad weather.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

zhǔyào is built from zhǔ 'to be in charge' and 要 'important', both inherited from Middle Chinese, tsyuX and 'jiewH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to manage, to lead' and the second 'to bind by agreement'.
One more word for saying what would happen.

lessons.title: 要么 (yàome) — either one or the other; either … or
lessons.gloss: either one or the other; either … or

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for to make conditions better, then the Mandarin for the main one.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: 要么

segments.text: 要么 — yàome — "either one or the other; either … or".
要么你来要么我去 yàome nǐ lái yàome wǒ qù — Either you come here or I go there.

要么 (yàome) is built from 要 and the light ending 么, as in 怎么. The first is inherited from Middle Chinese 'jiewH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription); the second is said light, and its history in this use is not settled.
One more word for saying what would happen.

segments.text: What set it off? (起因, qǐyīn.) As it turns out? (原来, yuánlái.) To result in something bad? (dǎozhì.) To cause damage? (zàochéng.) How well it works? (xiàoguǒ.) So as not to? (miǎnde.) And thereby? (cóng'ér.) In itself? (本身, běnshēn.) To arise from something? (chǎnshēng.) Not in the least? (gēnběn.) To stir up trouble? (rě.) To put the blame on? (怪, guài.) A strange business? (怪事, guàishì.) To come off worse? (chīkuī.) To get into trouble? (chuǎnghuò.) Eccentric? (古怪, gǔguài.) To drag someone into trouble? (liánlei.) Bound to happen? (nánmiǎn.) The whole chain of causes? (前因后果, qiányīn hòuguǒ.) What is going on here? (怎么回事, zěnme huí shì.) If it were not for? (要不是, yàobúshì.) It is thanks to? (duōkuī.) To make conditions better? (gǎishàn.) The main one? (zhǔyào.) Either one or the other? (要么, yàome.)
